key_provisions_or_claims: Policy, design and care scripts entwine, enabling and preventing use of feeding robots.
Danish policy promotes self-reliance; designers promote empowerment, but reality is more nuanced.
Care robots create choice-dependency situations for end-users and care providers.
Robots offer humble but important choices rather than realising bioethical principles.
Sustaining feeding robot use is difficult despite large-scale dissemination strategies.
annotation.summary_en: Ethnographic study in Denmark and Sweden of the Bestic feeding robot, using script theory to trace how policy strategies (self-reliance), design visions (empowerment) and care practices interact. It finds care robots create choice-dependency situations for users and care providers, making sustained use difficult yet sometimes useful.
annotation.title_clean: The entwinement of policy, design and care scripts: Providing alternative choice-dependency situations with care robots
